newsitem.title: CROATIA: No reasons for strike of Croatian railmen - agency.
newsitem.headline: No reasons for strike of Croatian railmen - agency.

text.p: The Croatian government said on Tuesday that railway workers had no reason to strike, state news agency HINA reported.

"Average salaries have reached the average wage rate in Croatian economy, as we promised," HINA quoted Transport Minister Zeljko Luzavec as saying. He added that wages rose 21 percent between December 1995 and August 1996.

The railway workers' union called for a general strike on November 28 after the government announced in its 1997 budget proposal that it would cut susbsidies to the loss-making HZ railway system to less than one billion kuna. The cut would rule out any possiblity of an additional pay rise.
HZ suffered damage worth $350 million during the war between the Croatian army and rebel Serb minority in 1991. Its traffic fell to one fourth of the pre-war level.
The Transport Ministry has asked the Canadian firm CANAC to help restructure HZ.
